observations: Photo 0: Front view of a Dell OptiPlex 990 desktop tower. The model name 'OPTIPLEX 990' is visible at the top. The front panel has a DVD drive, USB ports, and audio jacks. The Dell logo is visible below the drive bay. There are stickers for Intel Core i5 and Windows 7.
Photo 1: Same front view as photo 0, with clearer visibility of the 'OPTIPLEX 990' label and the Intel Core i5 sticker. The Dell logo is clearly visible.

Photo 2: Rear view of the same unit. Shows power switch, power connector, multiple ports including VGA, USB, Ethernet, and audio jacks. The case is dusty and shows signs of use. A blue VGA cable is connected.
The unit is placed on a wooden surface in what appears to be a workshop or storage area with other computer parts and boxes around.

claims.evidence: Model name 'OPTIPLEX 990' is clearly visible on the front panel in photo 0 and photo 1.
Intel Core i5 sticker is visible on the front panel in photo 0 and photo 1.
No power-on or operational photos. No screen or monitor shown. The unit appears dusty and in a workshop setting, but no proof of current functionality.
No visual evidence of origin or condition grade. The photos show dust and wear, which may contradict 'Grade A'. Location cannot be verified from photos.

risks.risk: The unit may not be functional or may have internal hardware failures.
risks.proof: A video showing the unit powering on, booting into Windows, and running a basic system check (e.g., CPU and RAM test).

risks.risk: The hard drive may be faulty or missing, or the system may not boot due to software issues.
risks.proof: A photo or video of the BIOS screen or Windows desktop after booting.

risks.risk: The unit may have been used in a harsh environment (e.g., workshop) and may have dust buildup or component wear.
risks.proof: A photo of the interior showing the motherboard, RAM, and cooling fans, with no visible dust or damage.
risks.if_unproven: priced as used with potential internal wear

proof_requests: Video of the unit powering on and booting into Windows.
Photo of the interior showing clean components and no visible damage.
Photo of the BIOS screen or Windows desktop to confirm functionality.
response.reason: The model and Core i5 processor are confirmed from visible stickers, but the claim of 'working perfectly fine' cannot be verified without proof of operation. The 'Grade A London Use' claim is unverifiable. Hidden risks include non-functionality, internal damage, or software issues. The item cannot be priced accurately without proof of working condition.
